import json
from pathlib import Path
import networkx as nx
from networkx.readwrite import json_graph

data = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/graph.json').read_text())
G = json_graph.node_link_graph(data, edges='links')

# find every esc-named node (AST may have one per file)
esc_nodes = [n for n, d in G.nodes(data=True) if d.get('label', '').lower().startswith('esc')]
print('esc() nodes found:')
for n in esc_nodes:
    d = G.nodes[n]
    print(f"  {n} | {d.get('label')} | {d.get('source_file')} | community={d.get('community')} | degree={G.degree(n)}")

print()
for n in esc_nodes:
    if G.degree(n) == 0:
        continue
    print(f'=== neighbors of {n} ({G.nodes[n].get("source_file")}) ===')
    for nb in G.neighbors(n):
        e = G.edges[n, nb]
        nd = G.nodes[nb]
        print(f"  --{e.get('relation')}--> {nd.get('label')} [{e.get('confidence')}] "
              f"({nd.get('source_file')}, community={nd.get('community')})")



================================================
FILE: docs/graph/_refresh.py
================================================
"""Post-commit graph refresh (AST-only, no LLM).

Re-runs the filtered detect + AST pipeline, preserves all semantic (doc/image)
nodes and edges from the existing graph, re-clusters, maps community labels
from labels.json by member overlap, and rewrites graph.json / graph.html /
GRAPH_REPORT.md in graphify-out/. Run from docs/graph/.

Doc/image changes are NOT picked up here - run /graphify <repo> --update for those.
"""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    here = Path(__file__).parent
    out = here / 'graphify-out'

    # 1. filtered detect + AST (both write dotfiles into cwd)
    for script in ('_detect.py', '_ast.py'):
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(here / script)], cwd=here,
                           capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            print(f'{script} failed:\n{r.stderr}')
            return 1
        print(r.stdout.strip())

    ast = json.loads((here / '.graphify_ast.json').read_text())
    old = json.loads((out / 'graph.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))

    # 2. preserve everything the new AST pass didn't re-extract (semantic layer)
    new_ids = {n['id'] for n in ast['nodes']}
    old_nodes = old.get('nodes', [])
    old_links = old.get('links', old.get('edges', []))
    preserved_nodes = [n for n in old_nodes if n['id'] not in new_ids]
    kept_ids = new_ids | {n['id'] for n in preserved_nodes}

    def endpoint(e, k):
        v = e.get(k)
        return v if isinstance(v, str) else v.get('id', v)

    ast_pairs = {(e['source'], e['target']) for e in ast['edges']}
    preserved_edges = []
    for e in old_links:
        u, v = endpoint(e, 'source'), endpoint(e, 'target')
        if u in kept_ids and v in kept_ids and (u, v) not in ast_pairs:
            # keep only edges with at least one preserved (non-AST) endpoint;
            # AST-to-AST edges are fully re-derived each run
            if u not in new_ids or v not in new_ids:
                preserved_edges.append({**e, 'source': u, 'target': v})

    extraction = {
        'nodes': ast['nodes'] + preserved_nodes,
        'edges': ast['edges'] + preserved_edges,
        'hyperedges': old.get('hyperedges', []),
        'input_tokens': 0, 'output_tokens': 0,
    }

    # 3. rebuild + recluster
    from graphify.build import build_from_json
    from graphify.cluster import cluster, score_all
    from graphify.analyze import god_nodes, surprising_connections, suggest_questions
    from graphify.report import generate
    from graphify.export import to_json, to_html

    G = build_from_json(extraction)
    communities = cluster(G)
    cohesion = score_all(G, communities)

    # 4. map labels from labels.json via member overlap with the old communities
    old_comm = {}
    for n in old_nodes:
        cid = n.get('community')
        if cid is not None:
            old_comm.setdefault(int(cid), set()).add(n['id'])
    saved = json.loads((here / 'labels.json').read_text()) if (here / 'labels.json').exists() else {}
    labels = {}
    for cid, members in communities.items():
        mset = set(members)
        best, best_ov = None, 0
        for ocid, omembers in old_comm.items():
            ov = len(mset & omembers)
            if ov > best_ov:
                best, best_ov = ocid, ov
        labels[cid] = saved.get(str(best), f'Community {cid}') if best is not None else f'Community {cid}'

    detection = json.loads((here / '.graphify_detect.json').read_text())
    gods = god_nodes(G)
    surprises = surprising_connections(G, communities)
    questions = suggest_questions(G, communities, labels)
    repo = str(here.parent.parent)
    report = generate(G, communities, cohesion, labels, gods, surprises, detection,
                      {'input': 0, 'output': 0}, repo, suggested_questions=questions)
    (out / 'GRAPH_REPORT.md').write_text(report, encoding='utf-8')
    to_json(G, communities, str(out / 'graph.json'))
    to_html(G, communities, str(out / 'graph.html'), community_labels=labels)
    # snapshot current labels keyed by NEW community ids for the next refresh
    (here / 'labels.json').write_text(json.dumps(
        {str(k): v for k, v in labels.items()}, indent=2))
    print(f'Refreshed: {G.number_of_nodes()} nodes, {G.number_of_edges()} edges, '
          f'{len(communities)} communities')
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(main())

FILE: docs/lidar/README.md
================================================
# OTB LiDAR — Orange Ocean Atlas / Cypress Command

USGS 3DEP elevation pack for the **On The Boulevard** deployment of
Orange Ocean Atlas. Atlas uses the DEM / hillshade on the **A-2 satellite
lens**. Cypress Command uses the LAZ alongside the existing splat / mesh
pipeline for 3D-roof work.

Binaries are **Release assets only** — not tracked in git (same spirit as
`public/OTB-splat.ksplat` and `public/OTB-mesh.glb`).

## Release

**[lidar-otb-v1](https://github.com/OrangeOnyx/otb-command/releases/tag/lidar-otb-v1)**
on `OrangeOnyx/otb-command`.

| Asset | Size | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `OTB-hillshade.png` (+ `.aux.xml`) | 132 KB | MapLibre overlay on A-2 satellite |
| `OTB-hillshade.tif` | 148 KB | Same hillshade as GeoTIFF |
| `OTB-dem-1m.tif` | 1.3 MB | 1 m COG for Atlas maps / analysis |
| `OTB-site.laz` | ~67 MB | ~10.5 M points — 3D-roof / Cypress Command |
| `METADATA.json` / `README.md` | — | Provenance |

## Fetch (local)

```bash
node tools/fetch-otb-lidar.mjs          # maps + DEM + hillshade → public/elevation/
node tools/fetch-otb-lidar.mjs --with-laz   # also the 67 MB LAZ (dev only)
npm run dev
```

Then A-2 → 🛰 Satellite. If the PNG is present, a **⛰ Relief** chip toggles
the hillshade over the frozen Esri base. If it is missing, the lens is
unchanged (quiet fallback) and the console notes the fetch command — prod
stays healthy with no elevation files deployed.

Idempotent: a second run skips files whose size already matches the Release.

Private-repo downloads use `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `GH_TOKEN` when set; public
browser URLs work without a token.

## Why the PNG is not in git

The hillshade PNG is 132 KB and MapLibre-ready. It stays Release-only so
Vercel stays lean and a missing `public/elevation/` directory cannot break
prod. The overlay **probes** `/elevation/OTB-hillshade.png` at lens open
(HEAD + content-type; Vite's SPA HTML fallback counts as absent).

To ship a default-on overlay later: copy the PNG into git (or a deploy
step). The probe already treats a committed file as present.

**Do not** put `OTB-site.laz` on Vercel. The fetch script omits it unless
`--with-laz`. `.vercelignore` excludes `public/elevation` as a belt.

## CRS / AOI

- **Clip AOI (WGS84):** west −92.056, south 30.199, east −92.050, north 30.205
  (center ≈ 30.20257, −92.05255 — Arnould Blvd / OTB).
- **DEM / LAZ CRS:** NAD83 / UTM zone 15N (`EPSG:26915`), 1 m pixels.
- **Hillshade overlay corners** (pixel-is-area extent → WGS84, for MapLibre
  `image` source) live in `src/data/elevation.json`.

The frozen satellite composite (`public/OTB-sat-base.jpg`) sits inside this
AOI; the hillshade is a slightly larger north-up drape.

## Source (public domain)

USGS 3DEP project **LA_Catahoula_Concordia_2017_D17** — U.S. Government work,
public domain. See the Release `METADATA.json` for tile URLs and clip notes.

Hillshade method (upstream): `gdaldem hillshade -z 1 -az 315 -alt 45`.

## Alongside splat / mesh

| Product | Path | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Hillshade / DEM | `public/elevation/` after fetch | Atlas A-2 relief overlay; map analysis |
| LAZ | `public/elevation/OTB-site.laz` after `--with-laz` | Cypress Command 3D-roof, not loaded by Atlas |
| Gaussian splat | `public/OTB-splat.ksplat` (`tools/convert-splat.mjs`) | A-2 🎥 Reality lens |
| Photogrammetry mesh | `public/OTB-mesh.glb` (`npm run mesh-glb`) | A-2 ◧ 3D mesh toggle |

The LiDAR pack does not replace the drone splat/mesh. DEM is the terrain
skin for Atlas maps; LAZ is the classified point cloud for roof geometry.

<h1>Cypress Command Platform — Property Onboarding Manual</h1>
<p><strong>Version September 2026 · the Phase C-1 rail, funnel-proven by the C-2 live run</strong>
Operator-driven by design — there is no self-serve signup. One intake file =
one property.</p>
<p>This is the complete procedure for bringing a new property onto the platform:
what to collect, how to build the intake file, how to run it (dry, then live),
how to verify the result, and what the new property's people do next. It ends
with the deliberate v1 fences and the teardown procedure.</p>
<hr />
<h1>1. What onboarding does</h1>
<p>A successful run creates, in one all-or-nothing transaction:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>The organization</strong> (management company) — or reuses it by slug if it
   already exists, so a second property lands under the same org.</li>
<li><strong>The property</strong> — slug, name, address, timezone, plus a <code>facts</code> list
   (label/value/source rows that dashboard-class cards derive from).</li>
<li><strong>The property settings row</strong> — ledger start month, renewal horizon,
   occupancy floor, late-fee schedule, and a free-form SOP settings object.</li>
<li><strong>The authorized-email list</strong> — email + role rows. No user accounts are
   forged: each person becomes real the first time they magic-link in, and
   the membership lattice assigns their role automatically.</li>
</ol>
<p>The moment it lands, the property appears as a card on <strong>D-0 Portfolio</strong>, and
— at two or more visible properties — the <strong>property switcher</strong> appears in
the sidebar for every org-wide member. Nothing else changes: rent posting and
API surfaces keep serving the default property until the new one is
deliberately activated.</p>
<p><img alt="D-0 Portfolio — each onboarded property is a card" src="img/portfolio.png" /></p>
<h1>2. What to collect before you start (intake checklist)</h1>
<p><strong>Org (management company)</strong>
- Slug (lowercase, hyphens — permanent, choose once) and display name.
- Brand kit if available (palette / wordmark / contact block) — may start
  empty <code>{}</code>.</p>
<p><strong>Property</strong>
- Slug (permanent), display name, street address, IANA timezone
  (e.g. <code>America/Chicago</code>).
- Facts worth surfacing: GLA, unit count, parking (with source citations —
  "rent roll 2026-08", "site plan"…). Facts are display rows, not schema;
  add what the owner will want to see.</p>
<p><strong>Settings</strong>
- <code>ledger_start_ym</code> (<code>YYYY-MM</code>) — the first month rent charges will post.
  Choose the first FULL month on the platform; historical balances are a
  data-package concern, not an onboarding concern.
- <code>renewal_horizon_days</code> (default 180), <code>occupancy_floor</code> (default 0.85),
  late-fee schedule (<code>late_grace_days</code> / <code>late_flat</code> / <code>late_per_day</code>).
- SOP answers (emergency policy, vendor rules …) — free jsonb under
  <code>settings.settings</code>.</p>
<p><strong>People</strong>
- Every email that should have access on day one, each tagged with a role:
  <code>operator</code> (full control) or <code>owner</code> (read-only, operator-curated sheets).
  Vendors and tenants are NOT onboarding rows — they come later through the
  vendor roster and tenant-login editor inside the app.</p>
<h1>3. Build the intake file</h1>
<h2>The easy way — the intake form (no technical knowledge needed)</h2>
<p><img alt="The fill-in-the-blank intake form" src="img/intake-form.png" /></p>
<p>Send the new property's manager the intake form link —
<strong>https://otb.cypresscommand.com/manual/intake-form.html</strong> (or email them the
file itself, <code>docs/phase-c/intake-form.html</code> — it works offline too). They
answer plain-English questions — company name, property name and address,
first billing month, late-fee schedule, who gets access — then click
<strong>⤓ Download intake file</strong> and send back the resulting
<code>intake-&lt;property&gt;.json</code>. The form checks its own answers as they go
(problems appear in plain English), auto-derives the permanent slugs from the
names, and cannot produce a file the validator would reject. It only prepares
the file — nothing is created until you run the rail in §4–5.</p>
<p>Anything they skip (facts, notes) you can add to the JSON afterward; their
free-text notes arrive under <code>settings.settings.intake_notes</code> for you to
translate into real SOP settings.</p>
<h2>The technical way — edit the JSON directly</h2>
<p>Copy the template and fill it in:</p>
<pre><code>docs/phase-c/onboarding-intake-template.json   →   docs/phase-c/intake-&lt;slug&gt;.json
</code></pre>
<pre><code class="language-json">{
  &quot;org&quot;: {
    &quot;slug&quot;: &quot;example-mgmt&quot;,
    &quot;name&quot;: &quot;Example Management, LLC&quot;,
    &quot;brand&quot;: {}
  },
  &quot;property&quot;: {
    &quot;slug&quot;: &quot;example-center&quot;,
    &quot;name&quot;: &quot;Example Shopping Center&quot;,
    &quot;address&quot;: &quot;100 Example Blvd, Lafayette, LA 70506&quot;,
    &quot;tz&quot;: &quot;America/Chicago&quot;,
    &quot;facts&quot;: [
      { &quot;label&quot;: &quot;GLA&quot;, &quot;value&quot;: &quot;50,000 SF&quot;, &quot;source&quot;: &quot;rent roll 2026-08&quot; },
      { &quot;label&quot;: &quot;Parking&quot;, &quot;value&quot;: &quot;250 spaces&quot;, &quot;source&quot;: &quot;site plan&quot; }
    ]
  },
  &quot;settings&quot;: {
    &quot;ledger_start_ym&quot;: &quot;2026-09&quot;,
    &quot;renewal_horizon_days&quot;: 180,
    &quot;occupancy_floor&quot;: 0.85,
    &quot;late_grace_days&quot;: 5,
    &quot;late_flat&quot;: 100,
    &quot;late_per_day&quot;: 25,
    &quot;settings&quot;: {}
  },
  &quot;authorized&quot;: [
    { &quot;email&quot;: &quot;operator@example.com&quot;, &quot;role&quot;: &quot;operator&quot; },
    { &quot;email&quot;: &quot;owner@example.com&quot;, &quot;role&quot;: &quot;owner&quot; }
  ]
}
</code></pre>
<p>Rules the validator enforces (the tool refuses to touch the database on any
error): slug shape, timezone shape, <code>YYYY-MM</code> ledger start, role whitelist,
fact and authorized row shapes. Reusing an existing org slug is legitimate
(that is how a portfolio grows); reusing an existing <strong>property</strong> slug under
the same org is refused.</p>
<h1>4. Dry-run</h1>
<pre><code class="language-bash">node tools/onboard-property.mjs docs/phase-c/intake-&lt;slug&gt;.json --dry-run
</code></pre>
<p>Validates the file and prints the full plan — org reuse vs create, the
property row, settings, and authorized emails — without any database contact.
Fix anything wrong and re-run until the plan reads exactly like the deal.</p>
<h1>5. Live run</h1>
<p>The live run uses the standard CRON_SECRET pull-load-delete drill (the secret
is pulled from Vercel env for the moment of use — never typed into chat,
never left on disk):</p>
<pre><code class="language-bash">node tools/onboard-property.mjs docs/phase-c/intake-&lt;slug&gt;.json
</code></pre>
<p>The RPC is all-or-nothing: any failure rolls the entire intake back. A
<strong>duplicate property raises</strong> (<code>P0001</code>) and clobbers nothing — this is the
protection, not an error to work around.</p>
<h1>6. Verify (two minutes)</h1>
<p><strong>In the app</strong> (as an org-wide member):
1. <strong>D-0 Portfolio</strong> shows the new property's card ($0 A/R, 0 work orders —
   correct for an empty property).
2. The <strong>property switcher</strong> now renders in the sidebar (it appears only at
   two or more visible properties).
3. Switch to the new property — every sheet boots <strong>empty</strong>. That is
   correct: a fresh property has no data package (§8).</p>
<p><strong>In SQL</strong> (Supabase console), if you want belt-and-suspenders:</p>
<pre><code class="language-sql">select p.slug, p.name, p.created_at, s.ledger_start_ym
from properties p join property_settings s on s.property_id = p.id
order by p.created_at;

select email, role from authorized_emails order by email;
</code></pre>
<p><strong>Financial isolation:</strong> the rent cron posts only to the default property;
<code>api/*</code> still resolves the flagship. A newly onboarded property cannot create
financial side effects until it is deliberately given a data package and
activated.</p>
<h1>7. First sign-ins</h1>
<p>Send each authorized person to the login page — they enter their email and
click the magic link; their membership row and role materialize on first
sign-in. Nothing to provision, no passwords to distribute.</p>
<p><img alt="The sign-in screen every counterparty uses" src="img/login.png" /></p>
<ul>
<li>The new <strong>operator</strong> lands with full control of their (empty) property.</li>
<li><strong>Owners</strong> land read-only on the operator-curated sheet set.</li>
<li>Anyone not on the authorized list lands on the pending screen with no
  data access — promote or ignore from the sidebar's access panel.</li>
</ul>
<h1>8. The v1 fences (deliberate — do not fight them)</h1>
<ol>
<li><strong>No data package.</strong> Onboarding creates the container, not the contents:
   units, geometry, rent roll, and seeds are the site-plan-tier premium step
   (Phase C data-package pipeline). Until that lands for the new property,
   the 17 property sheets remain bound to the flagship's bundled data — the
   new property renders correctly on D-0 and boots its own sheets empty.</li>
<li><strong>Known residual while switched:</strong> manual edits made while you are
   actively switched INTO a data-less property will sync to that property.
   Don't do data entry on a property that hasn't had its package built.</li>
<li><strong>No storage folder prefixes yet</strong> — the decision is deferred until the
   first real pilot's document volume makes the shape obvious.</li>
<li><strong>No self-serve UI.</strong> Governed, operator-driven onboarding is the
   deliberate wedge; a UI can wrap this rail later without changing it.</li>
</ol>
<h1>9. Teardown (removing a property)</h1>
<p>The C-2 proof property was created and torn down cleanly with this exact
pattern. Order matters (children first), and this is irreversible — read
twice, run once:</p>
<pre><code class="language-sql">-- any typed-layer/child rows first (comp_state, board_state, …), then:
delete from property_settings
 where property_id = (select id from properties where slug = '&lt;slug&gt;');
delete from properties where slug = '&lt;slug&gt;';
</code></pre>
<p>Then verify: D-0 shows one card fewer; the switcher disappears if only one
property remains; the flagship's data is untouched.</p>
<h1>10. Troubleshooting</h1>

# Cypress Command Platform — Property Onboarding Manual
**Version September 2026 · the Phase C-1 rail, funnel-proven by the C-2 live run**
Operator-driven by design — there is no self-serve signup. One intake file =
one property.

This is the complete procedure for bringing a new property onto the platform:
what to collect, how to build the intake file, how to run it (dry, then live),
how to verify the result, and what the new property's people do next. It ends
with the deliberate v1 fences and the teardown procedure.

---

# 1. What onboarding does

A successful run creates, in one all-or-nothing transaction:

1. **The organization** (management company) — or reuses it by slug if it
   already exists, so a second property lands under the same org.
2. **The property** — slug, name, address, timezone, plus a `facts` list
   (label/value/source rows that dashboard-class cards derive from).
3. **The property settings row** — ledger start month, renewal horizon,
   occupancy floor, late-fee schedule, and a free-form SOP settings object.
4. **The authorized-email list** — email + role rows. No user accounts are
   forged: each person becomes real the first time they magic-link in, and
   the membership lattice assigns their role automatically.

The moment it lands, the property appears as a card on **D-0 Portfolio**, and
— at two or more visible properties — the **property switcher** appears in
the sidebar for every org-wide member. Nothing else changes: rent posting and
API surfaces keep serving the default property until the new one is
deliberately activated.

![D-0 Portfolio — each onboarded property is a card](img/portfolio.png)

# 2. What to collect before you start (intake checklist)

**Org (management company)**
- Slug (lowercase, hyphens — permanent, choose once) and display name.
- Brand kit if available (palette / wordmark / contact block) — may start
  empty `{}`.

**Property**
- Slug (permanent), display name, street address, IANA timezone
  (e.g. `America/Chicago`).
- Facts worth surfacing: GLA, unit count, parking (with source citations —
  "rent roll 2026-08", "site plan"…). Facts are display rows, not schema;
  add what the owner will want to see.

**Settings**
- `ledger_start_ym` (`YYYY-MM`) — the first month rent charges will post.
  Choose the first FULL month on the platform; historical balances are a
  data-package concern, not an onboarding concern.
- `renewal_horizon_days` (default 180), `occupancy_floor` (default 0.85),
  late-fee schedule (`late_grace_days` / `late_flat` / `late_per_day`).
- SOP answers (emergency policy, vendor rules …) — free jsonb under
  `settings.settings`.

**People**
- Every email that should have access on day one, each tagged with a role:
  `operator` (full control) or `owner` (read-only, operator-curated sheets).
  Vendors and tenants are NOT onboarding rows — they come later through the
  vendor roster and tenant-login editor inside the app.

# 3. Build the intake file

## The easy way — the intake form (no technical knowledge needed)

![The fill-in-the-blank intake form](img/intake-form.png)

Send the new property's manager the intake form link —
**https://otb.cypresscommand.com/manual/intake-form.html** (or email them the
file itself, `docs/phase-c/intake-form.html` — it works offline too). They
answer plain-English questions — company name, property name and address,
first billing month, late-fee schedule, who gets access — then click
**⤓ Download intake file** and send back the resulting
`intake-<property>.json`. The form checks its own answers as they go
(problems appear in plain English), auto-derives the permanent slugs from the
names, and cannot produce a file the validator would reject. It only prepares
the file — nothing is created until you run the rail in §4–5.

Anything they skip (facts, notes) you can add to the JSON afterward; their
free-text notes arrive under `settings.settings.intake_notes` for you to
translate into real SOP settings.

## The technical way — edit the JSON directly

Copy the template and fill it in:

```
docs/phase-c/onboarding-intake-template.json   →   docs/phase-c/intake-<slug>.json
```

```json
{
  "org": {
    "slug": "example-mgmt",
    "name": "Example Management, LLC",
    "brand": {}
  },
  "property": {
    "slug": "example-center",
    "name": "Example Shopping Center",
    "address": "100 Example Blvd, Lafayette, LA 70506",
    "tz": "America/Chicago",
    "facts": [
      { "label": "GLA", "value": "50,000 SF", "source": "rent roll 2026-08" },
      { "label": "Parking", "value": "250 spaces", "source": "site plan" }
    ]
  },
  "settings": {
    "ledger_start_ym": "2026-09",
    "renewal_horizon_days": 180,
    "occupancy_floor": 0.85,
    "late_grace_days": 5,
    "late_flat": 100,
    "late_per_day": 25,
    "settings": {}
  },
  "authorized": [
    { "email": "operator@example.com", "role": "operator" },
    { "email": "owner@example.com", "role": "owner" }
  ]
}
```

Rules the validator enforces (the tool refuses to touch the database on any
error): slug shape, timezone shape, `YYYY-MM` ledger start, role whitelist,
fact and authorized row shapes. Reusing an existing org slug is legitimate
(that is how a portfolio grows); reusing an existing **property** slug under
the same org is refused.

# 4. Dry-run

```bash
node tools/onboard-property.mjs docs/phase-c/intake-<slug>.json --dry-run
```

Validates the file and prints the full plan — org reuse vs create, the
property row, settings, and authorized emails — without any database contact.
Fix anything wrong and re-run until the plan reads exactly like the deal.

# 5. Live run

The live run uses the standard CRON_SECRET pull-load-delete drill (the secret
is pulled from Vercel env for the moment of use — never typed into chat,
never left on disk):

```bash
node tools/onboard-property.mjs docs/phase-c/intake-<slug>.json
```

The RPC is all-or-nothing: any failure rolls the entire intake back. A
**duplicate property raises** (`P0001`) and clobbers nothing — this is the
protection, not an error to work around.

# 6. Verify (two minutes)

**In the app** (as an org-wide member):
1. **D-0 Portfolio** shows the new property's card ($0 A/R, 0 work orders —
   correct for an empty property).
2. The **property switcher** now renders in the sidebar (it appears only at
   two or more visible properties).
3. Switch to the new property — every sheet boots **empty**. That is
   correct: a fresh property has no data package (§8).

**In SQL** (Supabase console), if you want belt-and-suspenders:

```sql
select p.slug, p.name, p.created_at, s.ledger_start_ym
from properties p join property_settings s on s.property_id = p.id
order by p.created_at;

select email, role from authorized_emails order by email;
```

**Financial isolation:** the rent cron posts only to the default property;
`api/*` still resolves the flagship. A newly onboarded property cannot create
financial side effects until it is deliberately given a data package and
activated.

# 7. First sign-ins

Send each authorized person to the login page — they enter their email and
click the magic link; their membership row and role materialize on first
sign-in. Nothing to provision, no passwords to distribute.

![The sign-in screen every counterparty uses](img/login.png)

- The new **operator** lands with full control of their (empty) property.
- **Owners** land read-only on the operator-curated sheet set.
- Anyone not on the authorized list lands on the pending screen with no
  data access — promote or ignore from the sidebar's access panel.

# 8. The v1 fences (deliberate — do not fight them)

1. **No data package.** Onboarding creates the container, not the contents:
   units, geometry, rent roll, and seeds are the site-plan-tier premium step
   (Phase C data-package pipeline). Until that lands for the new property,
   the 17 property sheets remain bound to the flagship's bundled data — the
   new property renders correctly on D-0 and boots its own sheets empty.
2. **Known residual while switched:** manual edits made while you are
   actively switched INTO a data-less property will sync to that property.
   Don't do data entry on a property that hasn't had its package built.
3. **No storage folder prefixes yet** — the decision is deferred until the
   first real pilot's document volume makes the shape obvious.
4. **No self-serve UI.** Governed, operator-driven onboarding is the
   deliberate wedge; a UI can wrap this rail later without changing it.

# 9. Teardown (removing a property)

The C-2 proof property was created and torn down cleanly with this exact
pattern. Order matters (children first), and this is irreversible — read
twice, run once:

```sql
-- any typed-layer/child rows first (comp_state, board_state, …), then:
delete from property_settings
 where property_id = (select id from properties where slug = '<slug>');
delete from properties where slug = '<slug>';
```

Then verify: D-0 shows one card fewer; the switcher disappears if only one
property remains; the flagship's data is untouched.

# 10. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Meaning | Do |
|---|---|---|
| Validator errors on dry-run | Intake file shape is wrong | Fix the listed fields; nothing was sent |
| `P0001` duplicate raise on live run | Property slug already exists under that org | This is the no-clobber guard. Pick a new slug, or tear down the old property first |
| New property card missing on D-0 | Viewer is not an org-wide member | Check the viewer's membership; org-wide members see all properties |
| Switcher not visible | Only one property is visible to you | Correct at one property — it renders at two or more |
| Sheets look like the flagship after switching | You are looking at bundled flagship data | Expected until the property's own data package exists (§8) |
| Someone stuck on "pending" | Email wasn't in `authorized`, or typo'd | Add/fix via the sidebar access panel; they re-click a fresh magic link |

<h1>Cypress Command Platform — Operating Manual (On The Boulevard deployment)</h1>
<p><strong>Version September 22, 2026 · covers the 18-sheet production build (777 tests)</strong>
Live app: https://otb.cypresscommand.com (also orangeoceanatlas.com · otb-command.vercel.app) · Operator: adam@adamabdalla.com</p>
<p>This supersedes the July 2026 text-only edition (<code>docs/pitch/operator-manual.md</code>).
Every screenshot is a real capture of the running system. <strong>Tenant names and
dollar figures shown are representative sample data, not actual tenancy or
economics.</strong> Part I is orientation, Part II
is the operator's day, Part III covers each sheet in depth, Part IV is the
counterparty guides (owner / vendor / tenant / signer), Part V is the monthly
and periodic rhythms, Part VI is administration and recovery.</p>
<hr />
<h1>Part I — Orientation</h1>
<h2>1.1 Signing in</h2>
<p><img alt="The sign-in screen" src="img/login.png" /></p>
<p>There are no passwords. Enter your email on the login screen; a <strong>magic link</strong>
arrives by email; clicking it signs you in. Your role is resolved
automatically:</p>
<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>You are…</th>
<th>How the system knows</th>
<th>You land on</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Operator</td>
<td>adam@adamabdalla.com</td>
<td>Everything</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Owner</td>
<td>pre-authorized email (see §6.1)</td>
<td>Read-only, operator-chosen sheets</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Vendor</td>
<td>email matches the vendor roster</td>
<td>V-1 Vendor Portal only</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Tenant</td>
<td>email in the tenant-contacts list</td>
<td>M-1 Maintenance only, own unit</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Anyone else</td>
<td>—</td>
<td>A "pending" holding screen; no data</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p>If a legitimate person lands in pending, the operator promotes them (§6.1).</p>
<h2>1.2 The drawing-set metaphor</h2>
<p>The left sidebar is a <strong>sheet index</strong>, like an architect's drawing set:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>D-0 Portfolio</strong> — cross-property rollup (one card per property)</li>
<li><strong>D-1 Dashboard</strong> — KPIs, action queue, live cards</li>
<li><strong>A-1 Site Plan</strong> — the interactive plat</li>
<li><strong>A-2 Spatial</strong> — the property workspace (plat model, suite inspector, evidence) + capture lenses</li>
<li><strong>R-1 Rent Roll</strong> · <strong>C-1 Compliance</strong> · <strong>P-1 Financial</strong> — money and obligations</li>
<li><strong>S-1 Owner Safe</strong> — sealed document vault + property records</li>
<li><strong>AI-1 Concierge</strong> — the three AI personas</li>
<li><strong>T-1 Critical Dates</strong> · <strong>W-1 Action Board</strong> — what is due, who is doing it</li>
<li><strong>K-1 Directory</strong> — contacts, document register, pylon sign, site imagery</li>
<li><strong>B-1 Marketing</strong> — flyers, overview, tenant cards, photo library, tour media</li>
<li><strong>L-1 Comm Log</strong> — every letter, e-mail, meeting note and phone call</li>
<li><strong>N-1 Matters</strong> — long-running affairs with deadlines and correspondence</li>
<li><strong>M-1 Maintenance</strong> — work orders (also the tenant's sheet)</li>
<li><strong>O-1 Operations</strong> — the procedures (SOP) library</li>
<li><strong>V-1 Vendor Portal</strong> — vendor roster, COIs, work orders</li>
</ul>
<p>The masthead carries a <strong>KPI ribbon</strong> — Occupancy · Rent/mo · Vacant · Expiring ≤12 mo ·
Needs attention — and each figure is a button that drills into its sheet.</p>
<p>The URL tracks the open sheet (<code>#roll</code>, <code>#plan</code>…) — the back button walks your
history, and links can deep-link a sheet. Boot lands on D-1 (D-0 sits above it
in drawing-set order but is a rollup, not the daily surface).</p>
<h2>1.3 The unit drawer — the universal detail surface</h2>
<p><img alt="The unit drawer opened from the rent roll" src="img/drawer.png" /></p>
<p>Click any unit anywhere (site plan, rent roll, 3D lens, satellite) and the
<strong>drawer</strong> opens with everything about that unit: term progress, PSF economics,
HVAC responsibility, notes, contacts, documents, photos, compliance rows, the
<strong>Ledger</strong> panel, and the <strong>E-Sign</strong> panel. Most day-to-day work happens here.</p>
<h2>1.4 Search and shortcuts</h2>
<ul>
<li>Press <strong>/</strong> anywhere → omni-search units, contacts, documents; Enter opens
  the top hit.</li>
<li><strong>⤓ SHEET</strong> (topbar) or <strong>Ctrl+P</strong> → prints the open sheet as a stamped PDF
  (drawing-set footer, date, headline figures). R-1 is guaranteed one page.</li>
<li><strong>Export / Import</strong> (topbar) → full state snapshot as JSON; Import restores
  it. This is your portable backup (§6.4).</li>
<li>Theme toggle (sidebar foot): plan-room (default) ↔ dark. Print always
  reverts to paper.</li>
</ul>
<h2>1.5 Phones and tablets</h2>
<p><img alt="D-1 on a phone" src="img/mobile-dash.png" /> <img alt="The sheet index drawer on a phone" src="img/mobile-nav.png" /></p>
<p>At phone widths the sheet index becomes an off-canvas drawer behind the ☰
button, grids collapse to one column, and the unit drawer goes full-screen.
Everything works; nothing is mobile-only.</p>
<hr />
<h1>Part II — The operator's day</h1>
<p>A normal day touches five surfaces:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>D-1 Dashboard</strong> — scan the KPI row, the live cards, and the Action Queue
   (§3.2).</li>
<li><strong>W-1 Action Board</strong> — the kanban seeds <em>itself</em> from live facts
   (holdovers, renewal windows ≤12 months, vacancies, compliance flags,
   covenant obligations, open work orders). Drag cards between lanes, dismiss
   what's handled, add custom cards. You never have to remember to create a
   card for a lease expiring — it appears on its own.</li>
<li><strong>AI-1 History</strong> — the daily automated scan (11:00 UTC) may have opened a
   thread: a renewal window entered 180 days, a holdover appeared, occupancy
   dipped, the camera pipeline went quiet, a voice lead never booked, or a
   payment arrived that couldn't be matched. Each condition opens exactly
   <strong>one</strong> thread, ever — if there's nothing new, there's nothing there.</li>
<li><strong>M-1 Maintenance</strong> — new tenant requests (from the portal or the phone
   line) appear in the queue. Triage per §3.10.
4a. <strong>L-1 Comm Log</strong> — the "Calls · 7 days" strip and the attention filter:
   every recorded phone call with its summary, intent and urgency chips;
   listen, read the turns, then <strong>✓ Mark handled</strong> (§3.19).</li>
<li><strong>Mail/phone → the system</strong> — anything that arrived outside the system
   (a signed lease, a COI, a check conversation) gets recorded where it
   belongs the same day: SOT update (§5.3), vendor folder (§3.13), ledger
   entry (§3.11).</li>
</ol>
<hr />
<h1>Part III — Sheet-by-sheet instructions</h1>
<h2>3.1 D-0 Portfolio</h2>
<p>One card per property you can see: A/R outstanding (sum of positive unit
balances over effective ledger entries) and open work orders, with an as-of
stamp. "Open →" switches the active property. With a single property the
<strong>property switcher</strong> stays hidden; at two or more it appears in the sidebar
(see the onboarding manual). Derived — nothing to maintain here.</p>
<h2>3.2 D-1 Dashboard</h2>
<p><img alt="D-1 Dashboard" src="img/dash.png" /></p>
<p>Read-only KPIs derived from live data — nothing to maintain here. Cards:
occupancy/rent KPIs, parking variance (from the instruments file, not typed),
<strong>Parking Occupancy (C3)</strong> with 7-day trend (48-hour freshness window; the
as-of label shows date+time for non-today samples), <strong>Network (UniFi)</strong>
up/down, <strong>Automation (cron)</strong> — green with last-run age; brick-red STALE past
26 hours, which matters because maintenance aging, voice leads, C3 heartbeat,
UniFi, rent posting, and the owner brief all ride that one daily cron —
<strong>Client Errors (24h)</strong> (renders only when the count is nonzero), the
<strong>Calls</strong> KPI (recorded voice calls awaiting attention), and the
Action Queue (same cards as W-1). If a card shows brick-red, it is telling you
something needs attention.</p>
<h2>3.3 A-1 Site Plan</h2>
<p><img alt="A-1 Site Plan" src="img/plan.png" /></p>
<p>The recorded plat, interactive. A <strong>View</strong> row above the chips sets a preset
— Leasing · Daily Ops · Building Systems · Common Areas · Signage · Roof ·
Site / Hardscape — and the chips re-derive from it; toggling any chip by hand
drops the preset highlight. <strong>Chips</strong> toggle overlay layers:
- <strong>Lenses:</strong> Status / Expiry / Rent / Use / HVAC / Size — unit fills + legend.
- <strong>🅿 Parking</strong> — the 314 plat-labeled stalls by zone, plus the 10-stall Johnston
  row the CAD stripes but the plat never labels (marked as such).
- <strong>⇆ Access</strong> — ingress/egress as built: every curb cut drawn as an apron with its
  throat width, two-way arrow pairs at the cuts and along the aisles, the Arnould
  raised median and its one 55' opening (Driveway A is the only full-movement cut),
  edge-of-pavement lines, Lot 7's open Patricia frontage. Source: the architect CAD,
  satellite-confirmed (<code>docs/site-access-inventory-2026-09.md</code>).
- <strong>§ Easements</strong> — the §3a liquor line and its notes, the church easement note,
  10' utility easements, electric easement 577566, the 5×5' guy easement. Switch off
  for a clean leasing exhibit.
- <strong>🎥 Cameras</strong> — 17 mounts with view cones; click one → its live view.
  <strong>✎ Adjust cams</strong> (operator-only): drag pin to move, drag the brass dot to
  re-aim, double-click to reset; corrections persist.
- <strong>🚗 Occupancy</strong> — latest measured stall states painted green/outline over
  the storefront row, Lot 8 pocket, and the 149 corner.
- <strong>📍 Pins / ＋ Pin</strong> — drop a pin per water shutoff, meter, bench, column — and
  for lease/ops designations: reserved parking, monument-sign site, common area,
  loading zone, dumpster pad. Pins also appear on the satellite lens.
- <strong>Overlay → Floor plan</strong> — whole-center floor-plan raster under the unit
  boxes, with an opacity slider.
Click any unit → drawer.</p>
<h2>3.4 A-2 Spatial (four lenses)</h2>
<p><img alt="A-2 Spatial — iso lens" src="img/spatial.png" /></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Iso</strong> — SVG isometric, real CAD heights; ⇅ toggles true heights;
  ⤓ SVG exports a standalone file.</li>
<li><strong>◧ 3D</strong> — orbitable massing; <strong>🏗 Mesh</strong> swaps in the photogrammetry mesh.</li>
<li><strong>🛰 Satellite</strong> — frozen basemap with georeferenced footprints, unit
  labels, asset pins; opens plan-oriented (Marie Antoinette top).</li>
<li><strong>🎥 Reality</strong> — photoreal drone splat; ▦ toggles unit overlays; click a
  storefront → drawer.
All lenses share the same selection — pick a unit in one, it's selected in all.</li>
</ul>
<h2>3.5 R-1 Rent Roll</h2>
<p><img alt="R-1 Rent Roll" src="img/roll.png" /></p>
<p>11 sortable columns; any bare monthly amount is <strong>TOTAL rent</strong> (base +
additional). The PSF breakdown chart is the only place component economics
(Base · CAM · Tax · Ins) appear — by design.
<strong>⤓ SHEET</strong> prints the owner one-pager: guaranteed one page (the layout
measures itself and shrinks to fit), with expiry flags — ▲ brick ≤6 months,
△ amber 6–12 months — and a legend in the stamp.</p>
<h2>3.6 P-1 Financial</h2>
<p><img alt="P-1 Financial" src="img/fin.png" /></p>
<p>Income composition (bars + a composition donut beside the Base · CAM · Tax ·
Ins breakdown), rollover, and concentration charts; the <strong>NOI worksheet</strong>
(enter opex → NOI → cap-rate value) now opens with a <strong>revenue → NOI
waterfall</strong> (gross potential rent + vacancy are labeled ESTIMATES at the
effective PSF; expense steps are your worksheet lines only) and a <strong>cap-rate
sensitivity</strong> table ±100 bp in 25 bp steps around the entered rate (or the
flagged 8.50% appraisal reference when blank — never stored);
<strong>Collections &amp; aging</strong> (month collected-vs-charged, collections history bars,
and per-unit FIFO aging from the ledger); <strong>Tenant health</strong> — five tiles plus
a worst-first list with OK / Watch / At-risk chips and a "How this score is
calculated" fold (score model 60/25/15; rows open the drawer; hosted only);
and the <strong>CAM reconciliation</strong> card — year picker, prior-year opex worksheet,
per-tenant caps from the lease abstracts (<code>src/data/recovery-terms.json</code>),
derived occupancy gross-up, and a per-row <strong>⤓ Statement</strong> that prints the
tenant's annual reconciliation with the PSF breakdown, cap line and
methodology. Suites with unknown PSF print "Not determinable" rather than a
guess. The Excel proforma (<code>npm run proforma</code>) is the owner-overridable model
for underwriting conversations.</p>
<h2>3.7 C-1 Compliance</h2>
<p><img alt="C-1 Compliance" src="img/comp.png" /></p>
<p>A <strong>Document coverage</strong> card sits above the matrix: per occupied suite —
Lease · COI · COI expires · other documents — with filter chips and five
summary counts. Evidence = a file on the suite's document records OR a matrix
"On file"; a matrix Flag is a gap. Then the 11×27 matrix. <strong>Click a cell to cycle</strong> unknown → ok → flag → n/a
(food-service-only fields apply only where relevant). Every flip is recorded —
who, when, from→to — and <strong>⏱ History</strong> shows the trail. You cannot corrupt
this history; corrections are new flips. Edits sync live between devices —
flip a cell on your phone and it flips on the desktop without a reload.</p>
<h2>3.8 T-1 Critical Dates</h2>
<p><img alt="T-1 Critical Dates" src="img/dates.png" /></p>
<p>Three derived views — nothing to maintain:
- <strong>Lease expiry timeline</strong> — a four-year Gantt with a today line and bucket
  cards (past end · &lt;90 d · 90–180 d · &gt;180 d · term unresolved). Suites whose
  lease end is unresolved in the September 2026 lease review list under
  "term unresolved" with their review label — BY DESIGN, never guessed.
  Row click → drawer.
- <strong>Renewal pipeline</strong> — option terms transcribed from the executed leases
  (<code>src/data/renewal-options.json</code>, reference only; every notice = 60 days).
  Groups: Notice window · Deadline passed · Option available · Term
  unresolved. "Open suite" → drawer.
- <strong>Instrument + governance deadlines</strong> — the JD Bank servitude end, the
  insurance renewals, the premium-finance maturity, and every S-1 governance
  item with a date, on the same timeline as the leases.</p>
<h2>3.9 W-1 Action Board</h2>
<p><img alt="W-1 Action Board" src="img/board.png" /></p>
<p>See Part II. A <strong>leasing pipeline strip</strong> over the deals table (inquiry →
tour → proposal → signed; voice and web leads land here on their own) sits
above the lanes. Card types include seeded facts (holdover, renewal, vacancy,
compliance flag, covenant) and <strong>live work-order cards</strong> (<code>mr:</code> prefixed).
Overrides (lane moves, dismissals) persist; the seed recomputes every render,
so a dismissed card returns only if the underlying fact returns.</p>
<h2>3.10 M-1 Maintenance (operator face)</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Queue:</strong> every request with status, age, unit, photos.</li>
<li><strong>Assign:</strong> pick a vendor from the service roster → the vendor sees it in
  V-1 immediately.</li>
<li><strong>Status flips</strong> and notes are append-only events.</li>
<li><strong>Tenant logins:</strong> the roster editor (email ↔ unit) controls who may sign in
  as a tenant. Add email + unit; they magic-link in like everyone else.</li>
<li><strong>File on behalf:</strong> log a phone-in request yourself.</li>
<li><strong>Aging alarm:</strong> unassigned requests older than 2 days (1 for emergencies)
  open a manager thread automatically.
Tenant-side view: §4.3.</li>
</ul>
<h2>3.11 The Ledger (drawer → Ledger)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Balance headline + last entries with running balance.</li>
<li><strong>⤓ Statement</strong> — a branded, printable tenant statement (owner-visible).</li>
<li><strong>Prior payments</strong> — 13 months of payment history with status-truth
  lateness (the July 2026 rows imported from Asset Command were bulk-entered;
  never trust their paid-at dates).</li>
<li><strong>Lease abstract</strong> (operator-only panel) — the abstracted terms, escalation
  steps and option terms for the suite, beside the ledger.</li>
<li><strong>Monthly rent charges post themselves</strong> (idempotently) on the 1st, since
  August 2026.</li>
<li><strong>ACH payments post themselves.</strong> Each unit has a reusable Stripe payment
  link (ACH only; roster with URLs: <code>docs/stripe-payment-links-2026-08.md</code>,
  copy on Drive). You send the link through your own channel — the app sends
  nothing. When the payment settles (ACH takes days), the unit's ledger gains
  an <code>ach:&lt;payment-intent-id&gt;</code> entry automatically. A payment that can't be
  matched to a unit, or that fails, opens a manager thread in AI-1
  (<code>ach-unmapped:</code> / <code>ach-fail:</code>) instead of landing silently.</li>
<li><strong>"Payment received"</strong> records an out-of-band payment by hand.</li>
<li>Add charge / credit / adjustment / NSF / write-off as needed.</li>
<li><strong>Void</strong> = ✕ on an entry → creates a <em>reversing entry</em> (nothing is deleted).</li>
<li><strong>Late-fee chips:</strong> past the 5-day grace, a suggestion chip appears
  ($100 + $25/day, the standard schedule). It posts <strong>only when you confirm.</strong>
  If a lease carries different late terms, flag it — policy goes per-unit.</li>
<li><strong>Amount changes:</strong> re-run <code>tools/stripe-payment-links.mjs</code> for that unit
  and retire the old link in the Stripe dashboard.</li>
</ul>
<h2>3.12 The E-Sign panel (drawer → E-Sign)</h2>
<ol>
<li><strong>Create</strong> a request (optionally attach a document for review).</li>
<li><strong>Copy link / Copy message</strong> — the app sends nothing; you deliver the link
   through your own channel (text/email). This is deliberate.</li>
<li>The signer opens a plain, branded page — no login needed — reviews, and
   signs or declines (E-SIGN/LA-UETA consent language included).</li>
<li>You see the live status (sent → viewed → signed/declined/expired), can
   <strong>re-token</strong> (invalidate + reissue) or <strong>cancel</strong>, and get a signed receipt.
Tokens are single-lifecycle: double-signing or declining after signing is
rejected by the database itself.</li>
</ol>
<h2>3.13 V-1 Vendor Portal (operator face)</h2>
<ul>
<li>Roster (service vendors first, green "portal" tag = they can sign in).</li>
<li>Per-vendor private folder: upload / open / delete, all audited.</li>
<li><strong>COI tracking:</strong> set expiry + note per vendor → badge auto-classifies
  (expired / ≤30d / ≤60d / ok; missing is flagged for service vendors).</li>
<li><strong>🤖 Parse cert:</strong> drop an ACORD PDF → AI pre-fills carrier, limits, expiry,
  and a normalized note → review → <strong>Save COI</strong>. Always review before saving.</li>
<li>Assigned work orders appear on the vendor's face automatically (§4.2).</li>
<li><strong>Inviting a vendor</strong> = telling them to magic-link in with their roster
  email. Nothing else to configure.</li>
<li>Policy: COI / W-9 / license are verified at <strong>payment</strong>, not dispatch.</li>
</ul>
<h2>3.14 K-1 Directory</h2>
<p><img alt="K-1 Directory" src="img/dir.png" /></p>
<p>Property contacts (including the <strong>Property lines</strong> block — the tenant and
leasing numbers — and the insurance contacts: agent, brokers, claims lines),
the document register, and the site-imagery library. Register rows carry
<code>counterparty · amount · effective · matures · status · risk</code> besides the
file (📎 attach → the row's link becomes an "Open 📎" that always serves a
fresh secure URL); an <strong>expiring strip</strong> at the top lists what lapses next.
The <strong>pylon sign</strong> renders as a native SVG elevation next to the tenant
roster — hover links panel ↔ row, click → drawer; installed-but-unlisted
faces draw brick-dashed.</p>
<h2>3.15 S-1 Owner Safe</h2>
<p>Opens with <strong>Property records</strong>: a <strong>Risk register</strong> (worst-first) and a
<strong>Renewal &amp; maturity radar</strong> (soonest-first) derived from the document
register — today that is the 2026–27 insurance program as bound (property ·
BOP liability + umbrella · workers' compensation, all renewing 2027-05-15, the
premium-finance agreement maturing 2027-03-15), the loan maturity, the lender
title policy and the recorded instruments. Abstract of the bound policies:
<code>docs/insurance-program-2026-27.md</code>. Then the <strong>Governance</strong> block (items with
deadlines feed T-1), <strong>⤓ Board report</strong> (quarterly, assembled from the stored
owner briefs), and the category folders (Proforma / Leases / Tax / Insurance /
Banking / Other). Upload and open as the operator; owners read-only;
vendors/tenants sealed out at the database layer. <strong>Recent access</strong>
(operator-only) shows every view, upload, and delete with who and when.</p>
<h2>3.16 AI-1 Agent Desk</h2>
<p><img alt="AI-1 Concierge" src="img/ai.png" /></p>
<p>Three personas — <strong>🏛 Concierge</strong> (property Q&amp;A), <strong>🤝 Leasing</strong>,
<strong>🔧 Property Manager</strong> — all grounded in the property dossier + live state.
- Conversations persist and resume after reload; <strong>🗂 History</strong> reopens any
  thread; <strong>＋ New</strong> starts fresh.
- <strong>🎙</strong> mic input and <strong>🔊</strong> spoken replies (Chrome/Edge).
- <strong>Numbers are guardrailed:</strong> once a calculation is involved, every figure in
  the reply must trace to the deterministic engines or the reply is replaced
  with the engines' own summary. Ask the leasing agent things like
  <em>"compare retaining at $17 vs replacing at $20 with 3 months free and $10
  TI, 5-yr term, 1,917 SF, 7.5% cap"</em> — or the manager
  <em>"should I spend $45K on an RTU replacement with a $120K reserve, $30K/yr
  contributions, installed 2008, 15-yr life?"</em>
- <strong>📊 Briefs</strong> — the monthly owner-brief archive; Open 🔒 renders any month.
- <strong>📦 Lead SMS</strong> (leasing persona): copies a ready-to-send text with the
  public leasing one-pager (otb.cypresscommand.com/leasing.html) and the
  leasing line number. You paste and send it — the app sends nothing.
- <strong>Lease packages (operator-only):</strong> ask 🤝 Leasing to assemble a proposal;
  it collects terms conversationally, then generates a branded DRAFT proposal
  (and optionally the internal owner summary) as a card with <strong>Open 🔒</strong> and
  <strong>✉ Email</strong> (pre-filled mailto — you send it; it never auto-sends).
  Every generated document is DRAFT-stamped, subject to legal review.</p>
<h2>3.17 The voice lines (LIVE)</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Tenant line (337) 273-0384:</strong> 24/7; triages per the SOP (emergencies =
  leak / electrical / break-in / sewer → dispatch + notify after-hours, never
  wakes you for permission); files real work orders into M-1; never discusses
  eviction timelines.</li>
<li><strong>Leasing line (337) 270-7044:</strong> takes name + number, quotes the approved
  rate range only, screens against exclusive-use conflicts, books tour slots
  (18h lead, Tue/Thu defaults; double-booking is impossible). <strong>Truthful
  booking is enforced:</strong> the agent cannot claim a tour is booked unless the
  booking tool actually succeeded; an unbacked claim is corrected or replaced
  with an honest fallback, and a leasing call that ends without a booking
  opens a <code>voice-lead:</code> manager thread within hours so no lead drops.</li>
<li>Both greetings end "This call may be recorded." Every call is recorded at
  Twilio (once the Twilio account variables are set in Vercel), summarized
  the moment it ends (intent · urgency · unit · caller · callback · follow-up
  — nothing invented; hang-ups still record), written to <strong>L-1</strong> as a call
  card with the Caller/Agent turns and ▶ Play recording, mirrored as a
  transcript thread in AI-1 History, and e-mailed to the owners when a mail
  key is configured. Emergencies open a manager thread on their own.</li>
<li>The leasing line can <strong>send the leasing package</strong> by e-mail (and by text
  once A2P messaging is approved): the caller's request creates a deal row
  and the agent may only claim the legs that actually went out.</li>
<li>Calls that end before the summary lands are swept by the daily cron
  (≥20 minutes unfinalized) so nothing is lost.</li>
<li>Go-live steps + secret rotation drill: <code>docs/a3-voice-runbook.md</code>; call
  records: <code>docs/voice-call-records-runbook-2026-09-18.md</code>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>3.18 B-1 Marketing</h2>
<p>Five blocks, every one generated from the source of truth on the fly — a
flyer can never disagree with the rent roll, and <strong>rates are never printed</strong>:
1. <strong>Availability flyers</strong> — one printable flyer per vacant suite.
2. <strong>Center overview</strong> — stats · logo wall · site plan · availability.
3. <strong>Tenant cards</strong> — 1080-square co-marketing card per tenant.
4. <strong>Photo library</strong> — the assets bucket by suite; the operator picks the
   hero image per suite and the pick persists (<code>marketing</code> layer).
5. <strong>360° tour media</strong> — panoramas + hero stills uploaded to the PUBLIC
   <code>tour</code> bucket; <strong>Publish manifest</strong> refreshes what the /tour microsite
   shows. Insta360 export settings and the upload steps:
   <code>docs/marketing-b1-and-tour-2026-09-18.md</code>.
Every output opens as a page with Print / Save PDF. The <strong>pylon sign</strong> block
shows the sign, its roster and "tenants without a face" per tenant. QR codes
for the leasing page and the tour live in <code>public/qr/</code>.</p>
<h2>3.19 L-1 Comm Log</h2>
<p>The cross-channel correspondence sheet. Filter by channel (note / e-mail /
letter / meeting / SMS / voice / web) or unit, search, expand an entry,
hand-log new correspondence, delete stale rows. <strong>Voice rows</strong> (§3.17) carry
intent and urgency chips, a needs-attention dot, the summary, outcome links
(work order · tour · lead · package), ▶ Play recording, the Caller/Agent
turns, and <strong>✓ Mark handled</strong>. The "Calls · 7 days" strip and the attention
filter are the morning triage (Part II). Web tour requests from /tour land
here too. Owners see the log read-only, including every call's summary,
transcript and recording; tenants and vendors never see this sheet.</p>
<h2>3.20 N-1 Matters &amp; Planning</h2>
<p>Long-running property affairs as status-filtered cards: kind (lease
negotiation, claim, permit, dispute, project, general), status, deadlines,
correspondence and file attachments. Operator: open a matter, edit fields
inline, log meeting notes (they mirror into L-1), attach documents (they ride
the documents bucket), close or reopen. Deadlines feed T-1. Owners read the
cards and open attachments but never attach.</p>
<h2>3.21 O-1 Operations</h2>
<p>The procedures (SOP) library — categories → procedures → steps, with
due-today / overdue / streak state. Browse, expand a procedure, ✓ <strong>Complete</strong>
with notes and minutes (it closes the oldest open occurrence), author new
content (add or edit categories, procedures, steps; deactivate), clear stale
occurrences. The daily cron materializes each scheduled procedure's current
occurrence and opens ONE "SOPs overdue" digest thread in AI-1 keyed by the
newest lapse (a static backlog never re-fires). Owners read-only; tenants and
vendors never see O-1.</p>
<h2>3.22 The public /tour microsite</h2>
<p><code>otb.cypresscommand.com/tour</code> needs no sign-in: a 360° viewer per suite when
panoramas have been published from B-1, otherwise the plat, the numbers and
Call / Text-to-tour. The <strong>Request a tour</strong> form writes a web lead (deal row +
L-1 note, capped per day), opens a manager thread in AI-1, and e-mails the
owners when mail is configured. The leasing one-pager stays at
<code>/leasing.html</code>.</p>
<hr />
<h1>Part IV — Counterparty guides</h1>
<h2>4.1 Owners</h2>
<p>Sign in with your authorized email (the owner list is fixed by the operator —
§6.1). You see the sheets the operator has shared (dashboard, rent roll,
financials, and the Safe are typical), <strong>read-only</strong>. The Comm Log, when
shared, lets you listen to any recorded call and read its summary and
transcript.
The <strong>📊 Briefs</strong> panel in AI-1 holds your monthly intelligence brief — every
figure deterministic, archived permanently. You may ask the AI desk questions;
its numbers are guardrailed the same as the operator's.</p>
<h2>4.2 Vendors</h2>
<p>Magic-link in with the email the operator has on file. You see one sheet: your
own folder (your documents + "send a file to management"), your COI status
with a renewal nudge, and <strong>your assigned work orders</strong> — open each to read
notes and photos, add notes, and <strong>✓ Mark complete</strong> when done.</p>
<h2>4.3 Tenants</h2>
<p>Magic-link in with the email your management added. You see M-1 for <strong>your
unit only</strong>: file a maintenance request (describe the problem, attach photos),
watch its status, and <strong>"Your account"</strong> — your current balance and recent
ledger entries. Rent is paid through the payment link management sends you —
one link per unit, reusable every month. Emergencies (water leak, electrical
hazard, break-in, sewer): call the maintenance line rather than filing a
ticket.</p>
<h2>4.4 Document signers</h2>
<p>You'll receive a link from management. It opens a simple page — no account,
no app. Review the request (and the attached document if one is linked), then
sign or decline. The signature is recorded with timestamp and consent language
under the federal E-SIGN Act and Louisiana UETA.</p>
<hr />
<h1>Part V — Rhythms</h1>
<h2>5.1 Daily (mostly automatic)</h2>
<ul>
<li>11:00 UTC — proactive scan: renewals/holdovers/occupancy → AI threads;
  work-order aging; camera-pipeline heartbeat; rent-charge posting;
  unmatched-ACH threads; unbooked voice leads; UniFi outages; unfinalized
  voice calls swept into L-1; scheduled procedures materialized on O-1 and
  ONE "SOPs overdue" digest thread. The scan also
  stamps the <strong>Automation (cron)</strong> card on D-1 — if that card goes brick,
  every one of those safety nets is silent; treat it as urgent.</li>
<li>12:00 local + 23:45 local — camera frames classified + uploaded
  (hands-free; the sampler is watchdog-healed).</li>
<li>You: the Part II walk — dashboard, board, AI history, maintenance queue.</li>
</ul>
<h2>5.2 Monthly</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>1st:</strong> Owner Intelligence Brief generates itself; rent charges post
  themselves. Skim the brief before the owner does.</li>
<li>Send (or re-send) payment links through your channel; ACH payments post
  themselves as they settle; confirm or dismiss late-fee chips after the
  grace window.</li>
<li>Documented property walk (per SOP); update C-1 flags as found — the history
  logs itself.</li>
</ul>
<h2>5.3 When a lease is signed / a fact changes (governed SOT update)</h2>
<ol>
<li>Update the source of truth: <code>docs/lease-population-2026-09-10.md</code> and the
   suite's <code>leaseEvidence</code> in <code>src/data/units.json</code> (Tier 1 since the
   September 2026 lease review; <code>docs/sot-2026-07/</code> stays authoritative for
   suites the review does not name). Supersession rules:
   <code>docs/sot-supersession-2026-09-11.md</code>.</li>
<li>Apply the change to <code>src/data/units.json</code>. Leave a lease <code>end</code> BLANK when
   the signed documents do not resolve it — T-1 and W-1 then show "term
   unresolved" instead of a guessed date. No holdovers are assumed.</li>
<li><code>npm run split-seed</code> &amp;&amp; <code>npm run concierge-context</code> (the test suite fails
   if you forget — deliberately).</li>
<li><code>npm test</code> → commit → deploy (§6.3) → verify live.
Never trust an imported system's dates over signed paper; store stated-rent
exceptions as exceptions — do not "fix" them to formula.</li>
</ol>
<h2>5.4 Periodic</h2>
<ul>
<li>COI badges: chase at ≤60 days, escalate at ≤30 (§3.13).</li>
<li>Semi-annual house HVAC PM (the anchor unit is excluded — its lease requires
  the tenant to maintain its own HVAC with the designated contractor).</li>
<li>Move-out: solo walk + photos within 30 days; file to the unit's assets.</li>
<li>Re-run marketing artifacts when availability changes (<code>npm run poster</code>,
  leasing one-pager per <code>tools/leasing-package.py</code>).</li>
</ul>
<hr />
<h1>Part VI — Administration &amp; recovery</h1>
<h2>6.1 Granting and revoking access</h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Owner:</strong> sidebar → "Sign-in access…" → type email → <strong>+ Owner</strong>. Their
  first magic link lands them as owner. Anyone stuck in pending is listed
  there with one-click "make owner". Revoke = ✕ (removes pre-authorization;
  demoting an existing profile is a Supabase console step).</li>
<li><strong>Vendor:</strong> ensure their email is on the roster; tell them to sign in.</li>
<li><strong>Tenant:</strong> M-1 → Tenant logins → add email + unit. Remove the row to cut
  access.</li>
<li><strong>Owner sheet visibility:</strong> the "Owners can see…" panel controls which
  sheets owners get.</li>
</ul>
<h2>6.2 Quality gates (never skip)</h2>
<p><code>node --check</code> on changed modules · <code>npm test</code> (777) · <code>npm run build</code> ·
deploy · <strong>grep the prod bundle for the change</strong> · smoke the live URL.
Since 2026-09-11 <strong>every push to <code>master</code> deploys</strong> through
<code>.github/workflows/deploy.yml</code> (npm ci → npm test → vercel build/deploy
--prod); a failing test blocks the deploy. Verify by fetching the live page
and checking the <code>assets/main-&lt;hash&gt;.js</code> bundle name against the local build.</p>
<h2>6.3 Deploying</h2>
<p>Push to <code>master</code> (or merge a PR) — GitHub Actions deploys production. Manual
fallback from this machine:</p>
<pre><code class="language-bash">npx vercel deploy --prod --yes --scope adams-projects-0c52918e
</code></pre>
<p>(<code>.vercelignore</code> governs uploads — the 16MB splat + 3MB mesh ride in
<code>public/</code>.) Never promote a Preview deployment: previews run against the
isolated Supabase branch and the build aborts if production secrets leak into
the Preview scope.</p>
<h2>6.4 Backup &amp; portability</h2>
<ul>
<li>Topbar <strong>Export</strong> → full-state JSON. Take one before risky edits; <strong>Import</strong>
  restores.</li>
<li>The repo is the authoritative system; all exports (dossier, buyer set,
  posters) are disposable and regenerable. Every export also lands on
  <code>G:\My Drive\00 OTB\</code>.</li>
<li>A scheduled task (<code>OTB-Repo-Backup</code>, daily 03:00) bundles full git history
  to Drive. Committed-only — commit anything that matters.</li>
<li>Local preview without login: dev server on port <strong>5199</strong>; move <code>.env</code> aside
  temporarily — and restore it after. (Confidential rents do not render in
  that mode — by design.)</li>
</ul>
<h2>6.5 Secrets</h2>
<p>Keys live <strong>only</strong> in Vercel env — never in chat, repo, or disk. Rotations are
scripted drills: <code>tools/rotate-secret.mjs</code> (shared cron secret),
<code>tools/rotate-voice-secret.mjs</code> (voice). One-shot key needs (e.g. the
restricted Stripe key used to mint payment links) follow the drop-use-delete
drill: key to a dotfile, tool consumes it, file deleted — never in chat.
Vercel rejects env values with trailing whitespace at deploy time — the
scripts handle this; when feeding a secret to a CLI, use <code>cmd /c "… &lt; file"</code>
(PowerShell pipes append a newline).</p>
<h2>6.6 The camera (C3) pipeline</h2>
<p>Fully hands-free: sampler (5-min ticks, watchdog task self-heals it at logon
+ every 5 min) → midday 12:00 + nightly 23:45 classify + upload → app
surfaces. If it goes quiet 36 hours, a manager thread opens on its own. After
a machine reboot the watchdog relaunches the sampler; no manual step. Known
conventions: capture day-directories are UTC-keyed; frames live outside the
repo.</p>
<h2>6.7 Known limits (deliberate v1 boundaries)</h2>
<ul>
<li>E-sign, lease proposals, and payment links: the operator transmits
  links/documents; the app sends nothing outbound on its own.</li>
<li>Voice: no SMS notify on dispatch, no live call transfer, no daily call cap
  (set a Twilio usage trigger); recordings and the leasing-package e-mail
  wait on the Twilio and mail keys in Vercel; the leasing package by text
  waits on A2P approval; settings edits via SQL until a UI lands.</li>
<li>B-1 outputs and the /tour site never print a rate; the operator quotes
  rates in person or by the leasing line's approved range.</li>
<li>Desktop-first; the phone experience is a responsive web app, not a native
  app.</li>
<li>Onboarding a second property is operator-driven (see the onboarding
  manual); there is no self-serve signup.</li>
</ul>
<hr />
<p><em>Questions the manual doesn't answer: ask the 🏛 Concierge — it is grounded in
the same governed data this manual describes.</em></p>
